Where is Yukon, Oklahoma, and how is it laid out?

Yukon sits in east central Canadian County, west of Oklahoma City. The city has about 26.5 square miles of land, and downtown Oklahoma City is roughly 16 miles to the east.

Route 66 and state highways 4 and 92 run through town, and Interstate 40 lies just south. The city line meets the Oklahoma City boundary about 3.5 miles east of the center of Yukon. Oklahoma City annexed nearly all the land around Yukon during the 1960s, which set off a boom in residential construction (Wikipedia).

Two ZIP codes, 73085 and 73099, cover the city.

What is the short history of Yukon?

Yukon was platted on February 14, 1891 by A.N. Spencer, a Texas cattleman turned railroad builder, and voters incorporated the town in 1901.

The town took its name from the Yukon River. Czech and Bohemian immigrants began arriving around 1898, and Yukon still calls itself the Czech Capital of Oklahoma. The Yukon Mill and Grain Company opened in 1893 and by 1915 was shipping flour and feed across the South and overseas. Voters approved water works, sewer and electricity in 1910, and the city grew from 3,076 people in 1960 to 8,411 in 1970 and 17,112 in 1980.

The Oklahoma Czech Festival parade runs directly on Route 66. The Festival Committee lists the 2026 event, its 60th, for October 2 and 3 and ties it to the Route 66 centennial (Oklahoma Czech Festival).

What is the economy like around Yukon?

Yukon works mostly as a bedroom community for the Oklahoma City area. Wikipedia describes it as primarily a residential community for people who work in the metro, after a long history as a farm-service and milling town.

The City of Yukon's economic development page reports a workforce unemployment rate of 2.6% and an average commute of 22.5 minutes, alongside a 2022 population estimate of 25,556. The city also runs an Economic Development Authority, created by the council on August 6, 2013 to finance and manage investment projects in or near Yukon (City of Yukon).

Which school districts serve Yukon homes?

Yukon Public Schools covers most of the city, but parts of Yukon are zoned to Banner Public School and Riverside Public School instead.

The Oklahoma State Department of Education transparency site lists the Yukon district at 600 Maple Street, with 9,597 students on October 1 of the 2024-25 year. Yukon High School, at 1777 South Yukon Parkway, reported 2,984 students, and Yukon Middle School, at 801 Garth Brooks Boulevard, reported 1,410. Wikipedia counts 11 schools in the district.

If you sell, check which district your address falls in. Buyers ask, and the answer is not always the one the mailing address suggests.

How do Oklahoma storms affect a Yukon house and its sale?

Hail and wind are the most common roof issue for Oklahoma homeowners, and they shape inspections on Yukon sales. The Oklahoma Insurance Department says hail damage is the most common homeowners claim type and that policies can carry a separate wind or hail deductible in higher-risk areas.

The same agency notes that many insurers offer discounts for impact-resistant roofing, and its OKReady program promotes FORTIFIED roof standards for wind and hail mitigation (Oklahoma Insurance Department).

  • Keep roofing invoices, claim paperwork and any impact-resistant shingle documentation.
  • Read your policy for a separate wind or hail deductible before deciding whether to repair or sell as-is.

What permits and inspections does the City of Yukon handle?

The City of Yukon Development Services office issues building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits, and it takes inspection requests at 405-354-6676, Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The city's residential permit page states that its fee schedule does not include state-mandated charges, and that every permit adds a $4 state fee and a $0.50 city collection fee. Projects such as pools and pipelines need a full set of plans, including a plot plan, with the application (City of Yukon permits).

If you did work yourself, such as a finished garage or a new deck, find out whether it was permitted before a buyer's inspector asks.

How do I handle Yukon utilities when I sell?

Yukon water service is run through the city's Utility Billing department, which reads meters monthly and handles start, stop and transfer requests.

The department's page lists links for starting service, stopping service and transferring service, plus a deposit return request form. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., with a main line at 405-350-3910 and an automated payment line at (405) 864-0016. Landlords have a separate authorization form to reactivate accounts (City of Yukon Utility Billing).

Schedule the stop or transfer for your closing date, and keep the final meter read with your closing papers. If a tenant had the account, confirm it is paid up before you hand over the keys.

What does Oklahoma law require a Yukon seller to disclose?

Oklahoma's Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act applies when a seller of a one or two unit home uses a real estate licensee, or receives a written request from the buyer for a disclosure or disclaimer.

The seller either delivers a disclosure statement or a disclaimer, and it must reach the buyer before an offer is accepted. The form covers items such as water and sewer systems, flood zone status, the roof, walls and foundation, wood-destroying insects, and major fire or tornado damage. A statement may not be dated more than 180 days before the buyer receives it (Oklahoma Real Estate Commission, 60 O.S. 831 to 839).

  • A seller who never lived in the house can sign a disclaimer stating they have no actual knowledge of defects.
  • If you learn of a new defect after delivering the form, you must promptly deliver an amended one.
  • The act exempts several transfers, including those by a fiduciary who is not an owner-occupant in an estate, trust or guardianship, and transfers after foreclosure.

Who bills property tax on a Yukon house?

Yukon is billed through Canadian County. The county assessor values the property, and the Canadian County Treasurer, with offices at 314 W. Rogers Street in El Reno, collects the tax.

The Treasurer's site says the treasurer collects taxes certified by the assessor and distributes them to the county, cities, towns and schools. It also says special assessments that cities originally assess, such as weed, cleaning, paving and nuisance abatement charges, are certified to the Treasurer once delinquent and placed as a lien on the property tax account. Online payment fees are 1.95% for debit cards, 2.75% for credit cards and $1.50 for an eCheck, and a returned check costs $35 (Canadian County Treasurer).

Before you list, look up the parcel on the treasurer's tax roll site and confirm there is no delinquent balance or city lien. The Treasurer's office is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. at 405-295-6330.

Is Yukon, OK in Oklahoma County or Canadian County?

Which taxes do I owe when I sell a Yukon house?

Property tax for the year is the main one. How the current year is split between you and the buyer is set in the sale contract and handled by the title company, so check your closing statement.

Do I have to give a buyer a condition report in Yukon?

Usually yes. Oklahoma requires a seller of a one or two unit home to give a written disclosure or disclaimer before an offer is accepted when a real estate licensee is involved or the buyer asks in writing. Several transfers are exempt, such as those by a non-occupant fiduciary in an estate.

Can I sell a Yukon house with storm damage?
